LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.learnerPromise: Describe two qualities or abilities that are true at the same time.
LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.explanation: Put 又 before each quality: 又快又方便. Both sides describe the same person or thing, and they match in shape. Use 又…又… for two qualities that are true at the same time — not for two things.

teachingGlossary.meaning: do not have; there is not

LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.pattern: Person or thing + 又 + quality 1 + 又 + quality 2

patternRows.english: The MRT is both fast and convenient.
A taxi is both fast and comfortable.
She is both cute and pretty.

items.question: Do I need 又 twice for "fast and convenient"?
items.answer: Yes — one 又 for each quality: 又快又方便. Each quality gets its own 又.

right.english: The MRT is fast and convenient.

items.question: Can I say 附近又學校又店 for "there is a school and a shop nearby"?
items.answer: No. 又…又… pairs qualities, not places or things. For two places, use 有…也有…: 附近有學校，也有店.

right.pinyin: Fùjìn yǒu xuéxiào, yě yǒu diàn.
right.english: There is a school and a shop nearby.

items.question: Can I mix 又 and 也 — 公車又快也便宜?
items.answer: No. Pair both qualities with 又: 又快又便宜. 也 adds a separate point; it does not build the pair.

right.english: The bus is fast and cheap.

discoveryLab.title: Balance the two sides
discoveryLab.description: Each 又 opens one matching description. Both sides describe the same person or thing.

choices.label: Transit
choices.traditional: 臺北的捷運又快又方便。
choices.simplified: 台北的捷运又快又方便。
choices.pinyin: Táiběi de jiéyùn yòu kuài yòu fāngbiàn.
choices.english: Taipei’s MRT is fast and convenient.
choices.note: 快 and 方便 are two matching qualities.

choices.label: Person
choices.traditional: 我同學的妹妹又可愛又漂亮。
choices.simplified: 我同学的妹妹又可爱又漂亮。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ tóngxué de mèimei yòu kě’ài yòu piàoliang.
choices.english: My classmate’s younger sister is cute and pretty.
choices.note: One person has both qualities.

choices.label: Two states
choices.traditional: 我現在又餓又渴。
choices.simplified: 我现在又饿又渴。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài yòu è yòu kě.
choices.english: I am both hungry and thirsty now.
choices.note: Both body states are true together.

choices.label: Repair balance
choices.traditional: 捷運又快方便 → 捷運又快又方便
choices.simplified: 捷运又快方便 → 捷运又快又方便
choices.pinyin: Jiéyùn yòu kuài fāngbiàn → Jiéyùn yòu kuài yòu fāngbiàn
choices.english: The MRT is both fast and convenient.
choices.note: Give each quality its own 又.

discoveryLab.takeaway: One person or thing, two matching 又 blocks.

text.traditional: 這家飯店又便宜又舒服。
text.simplified: 这家饭店又便宜又舒服。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiā fàndiàn yòu piányi yòu shūfu.
text.english: This hotel is inexpensive and comfortable.

text.traditional: 坐計程車又快又方便，可是比較貴。
text.simplified: 坐计程车又快又方便，可是比较贵。
text.pinyin: Zuò jìchéngchē yòu kuài yòu fāngbiàn, kěshì bǐjiào guì.
text.english: Taking a taxi is fast and convenient, but more expensive.

text.traditional: 元真又會唱歌又會跳舞。
text.simplified: 元真又会唱歌又会跳舞。
text.pinyin: Yuánzhēn yòu huì chànggē yòu huì tiàowǔ.
text.english: Yuanzhen can both sing and dance.

text.traditional: 我現在又累又渴，想先休息。
text.simplified: 我现在又累又渴，想先休息。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài yòu lèi yòu kě, xiǎng xiān xiūxí.
text.english: I am tired and thirsty now and want to rest first.

LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.exerciseInstruction: Choose a complete 又…又… pair for each scene.

questions.correctFeedback: Both qualities get their own 又.
questions.repairFeedback: Build 又 + 快 + 又 + 方便.

segments.hint: Put 又 immediately before each quality.

questions.correctFeedback: The hotel has both qualities.
questions.repairFeedback: Put 又 immediately before each quality.

segments.hint: Use one 又 before 餓 and one before 渴.

questions.correctFeedback: Both new body states are true together.
questions.repairFeedback: Use one 又 before 餓 and one before 渴.

LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.learnerPromise: Name an activity first, then comment on it.
LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.explanation: In Chinese, you can say the activity first, then say what you think about it. Think: activity → your comment.

teachingGlossary.meaning: do not have; there is not

patternRows.english: Taking the MRT is convenient.
Walking there is too slow.
I like both running and swimming.

items.question: In English I say "It’s convenient to take the MRT." Does Chinese copy that order?
items.answer: No. Say the activity first, then the comment: 坐捷運很方便. The activity is what you are talking about; the comment follows.

items.question: Do I need 是 between the activity and the comment — 走路去是太慢了?
items.answer: No. Put the activity first and the describing word right after it: 走路去太慢了. 是 is not needed here.

items.question: I like running, swimming, and tennis. Where does 都 go?
items.answer: Right after the person, before the action: 我都喜歡. Never after the verb: 我喜歡都跑步 is wrong.

right.traditional: 跑步、游泳、打網球，我都喜歡。
right.simplified: 跑步、游泳、打网球，我都喜欢。
right.pinyin: Pǎobù, yóuyǒng, dǎ wǎngqiú, wǒ dōu xǐhuān.
right.english: Running, swimming, and tennis — I like them all.

discoveryLab.title: Put the activity on stage
discoveryLab.description: The first chunk is what we are talking about; the rest is the comment.

choices.label: MRT
choices.traditional: 坐捷運很方便。
choices.simplified: 坐捷运很方便。
choices.pinyin: Zuò jiéyùn hěn fāngbiàn.
choices.english: Taking the MRT is convenient.
choices.note: 坐捷運 is the activity topic; 很方便 is the comment.

choices.label: Walking
choices.traditional: 走路去太慢了。
choices.simplified: 走路去太慢了。
choices.pinyin: Zǒulù qù tài màn le.
choices.english: Walking there is too slow.
choices.note: 走路去 is evaluated as one complete activity.

choices.label: Three sports
choices.traditional: 跑步、游泳、打網球，我都喜歡。
choices.simplified: 跑步、游泳、打网球，我都喜欢。
choices.pinyin: Pǎobù, yóuyǒng, dǎ wǎngqiú, wǒ dōu xǐhuān.
choices.english: Running, swimming, and tennis—I like them all.
choices.note: Several activities can share one comment.

choices.label: Repair focus
choices.traditional: 很方便坐捷運 → 坐捷運很方便
choices.simplified: 很方便坐捷运 → 坐捷运很方便
choices.pinyin: Hěn fāngbiàn zuò jiéyùn → Zuò jiéyùn hěn fāngbiàn
choices.english: Taking the MRT is convenient.
choices.note: Put the activity before the comment.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Activity first, comment second. You do not need 是 between them.

text.traditional: 坐公車很便宜，可是有一點慢。
text.simplified: 坐公车很便宜，可是有一点慢。
text.pinyin: Zuò gōngchē hěn piányi, kěshì yǒu yìdiǎn màn.
text.english: Taking the bus is inexpensive, but a little slow.

text.traditional: 走路去太慢了，我們坐捷運吧。
text.simplified: 走路去太慢了，我们坐捷运吧。
text.pinyin: Zǒulù qù tài màn le, wǒmen zuò jiéyùn ba.
text.english: Walking is too slow; let’s take the MRT.

text.traditional: 唱歌、跳舞，她都喜歡。
text.simplified: 唱歌、跳舞，她都喜欢。
text.pinyin: Chànggē, tiàowǔ, tā dōu xǐhuān.
text.english: Singing and dancing—she likes both.

text.traditional: 住在學校附近很方便。
text.simplified: 住在学校附近很方便。
text.pinyin: Zhù zài xuéxiào fùjìn hěn fāngbiàn.
text.english: Living near school is convenient.

LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.exerciseInstruction: Choose the sentence that clearly introduces an activity before evaluating it.

segments.hint: Use activity + comment without 是.

questions.correctFeedback: The activity leads and the comment lands after it.
questions.repairFeedback: Use activity + comment without 是.

segments.hint: Keep the whole activity before 太慢了.

questions.correctFeedback: 走路去 stays together as the topic.
questions.repairFeedback: Keep the whole activity before 太慢了.

segments.hint: Put 都 right after the person: 我都喜歡.

questions.correctFeedback: 都 gathers every listed activity into one comment.
questions.repairFeedback: Put 都 right after the person: 我都喜歡.

LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.titleEnglish: Draw a Route with 從 and 到
LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.learnerPromise: Say where a trip starts, where it ends, and why someone travels.
LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.explanation: 從 is the start pin. 到 is the destination pin. Put each place right after its pin. Finish with 來 or 去. You can add the purpose (the why) at the end.

teachingGlossary.meaning: do not have; there is not

LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.pattern: Person + 從 + start + 到 + destination + 來/去 + purpose

patternRows.english: Go from school to the drink shop to buy something.
Come from the hotel to my home to eat.
Come from Korea to Taiwan to visit a friend.

items.question: I want to say "I go from home to school." Which place comes right after 從?
items.answer: The start — the place you leave. 從 + start, 到 + destination: 我從家到學校去.

right.pinyin: Wǒ cóng jiā dào xuéxiào qù.
right.english: I go from home to school.

items.question: My friend is at the hotel and I am at home. She is coming to my place — 來 or 去?
items.answer: 來. Use 來 when the trip ends where you are; 去 points away from you. Her trip ends at my home, so: 她從飯店到家來.

right.pinyin: Tā cóng fàndiàn dào jiā lái.
right.english: She comes from the hotel to my home.

items.question: English says "go to school." Why is 我去到學校 not right in Chinese?
items.answer: Because 去 already means go, and 到 points at the destination. Chinese puts the place between them: 我到學校去.

routeLab.title: Move the route pins
routeLab.description: Read each trip left to right. Start, destination, direction, then purpose.

choices.label: Go to class
choices.traditional: 我從家到學校去上課。
choices.simplified: 我从家到学校去上课。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ cóng jiā dào xuéxiào qù shàngkè.
choices.english: I go from home to school for class.
choices.note: 從 opens the start. 到 opens the destination. 去 points away from the speaker.

choices.label: Mail a letter
choices.traditional: 我從學校到郵局去寄信。
choices.simplified: 我从学校到邮局去寄信。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ cóng xuéxiào dào yóujú qù jì xìn.
choices.english: I go from school to the post office to mail a letter.
choices.note: The purpose 寄信 comes after the complete route.

choices.label: Visit a friend
choices.traditional: 她從韓國到臺灣來看朋友。
choices.simplified: 她从韩国到台湾来看朋友。
choices.pinyin: Tā cóng Hánguó dào Táiwān lái kàn péngyǒu.
choices.english: She comes from Korea to Taiwan to visit a friend.
choices.note: Use 來 because the trip moves toward the speaker’s viewpoint.

routeLab.takeaway: Pins stay paired: 從 + start, 到 + destination. 來/去 shows which way the trip points, not the vehicle.

text.traditional: A：你從哪裡來？ B：我從飯店來。
text.simplified: A：你从哪里来？ B：我从饭店来。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ cóng nǎlǐ lái? B: Wǒ cóng fàndiàn lái.
text.english: A: Where are you coming from? B: From the hotel.

text.traditional: A：你到哪裡去？ B：我到朋友家去。
text.simplified: A：你到哪里去？ B：我到朋友家去。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ dào nǎlǐ qù? B: Wǒ dào péngyǒu jiā qù.
text.english: A: Where are you going? B: To my friend’s home.

text.traditional: 我們從學校到超市去買東西。
text.simplified: 我们从学校到超市去买东西。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen cóng xuéxiào dào chāoshì qù mǎi dōngxi.
text.english: We go from school to the supermarket to shop.

examples.teachingNote: Use 來 for motion toward here.

text.traditional: 他明天從飯店到我家來吃飯。
text.simplified: 他明天从饭店到我家来吃饭。
text.pinyin: Tā míngtiān cóng fàndiàn dào wǒ jiā lái chīfàn.
text.english: Tomorrow he will come from the hotel to my home for dinner.

LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.exerciseInstruction: Build each trip in route order. Tap a tile, then the blank.

segments.hint: Keep 從 with the start and 到 with the destination.

cóng jiā qù dào xuéxiào shàngkè

tiles.traditional: 從韓國到臺灣來看朋友

tiles.traditional: 從韓國來到臺灣看朋友

LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.learnerPromise: Put 了 at the end when a new situation becomes true.
LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.explanation: Put 了 at the end of the sentence when something new happens. Before, it was not true; now it is. 了 can come after a feeling, a time, an arrival, or a new chance to act. 了 does not mean "past time".

teachingGlossary.meaning: do not have; there is not

patternRows.english: I have become tired.
It is ten o’clock now.
The bus is here; we can board now.

items.question: Your stomach just started growling. Which tells people "I have become hungry"?
items.answer: 我餓了. 了 says the hungry state is new; 我很餓 only describes how hungry you are.

items.question: The bus is here and we can board. Where does 了 go in 我們可以上車?
items.answer: At the very end: 我們可以上車了. 了 closes the whole new situation — not between 可以 and 上車.

right.english: We can board the bus now.

items.question: Someone asks if you are tired now, after the long walk. Do you answer 我昨天累了?
items.answer: No — that says you were tired yesterday. Say 我現在累了: 了 marks the change, and the time word tells when.

discoveryLab.title: Ring the change bell
discoveryLab.description: See the moment when a state becomes true for the first time.

choices.label: Hungry now
choices.traditional: 我餓了。
choices.simplified: 我饿了。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ è le.
choices.english: I’m hungry now.
choices.note: The speaker was not hungry before; that state has changed.

choices.label: Bus arrived
choices.traditional: 公車來了。
choices.simplified: 公车来了。
choices.pinyin: Gōngchē lái le.
choices.english: The bus is here now.
choices.note: The arrival creates a new situation.

choices.label: Time changed
choices.traditional: 現在十點了。
choices.simplified: 现在十点了。
choices.pinyin: Xiànzài shí diǎn le.
choices.english: It’s ten now.
choices.note: The clock has reached a new reference point.

choices.label: Repair meaning
choices.traditional: 昨天我累了 → 我現在累了
choices.simplified: 昨天我累了 → 我现在累了
choices.pinyin: Zuótiān wǒ lèi le → Wǒ xiànzài lèi le
choices.english: I am tired now.
choices.note: For this target meaning, make the changed situation current and clear.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Use 了 when "now it is different" matters.

text.traditional: 我累了，不想走了。
text.simplified: 我累了，不想走了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ lèi le, bù xiǎng zǒu le.
text.english: I’m tired now and no longer want to walk.

text.traditional: 公車來了，我們可以上車了。
text.simplified: 公车来了，我们可以上车了。
text.pinyin: Gōngchē lái le, wǒmen kěyǐ shàngchē le.
text.english: The bus is here; now we can board.

text.traditional: 現在十點了，我們先回家吧。
text.simplified: 现在十点了，我们先回家吧。
text.pinyin: Xiànzài shí diǎn le, wǒmen xiān huí jiā ba.
text.english: It’s ten now; let’s go home first.

text.traditional: 她渴了，想先買飲料。
text.simplified: 她渴了，想先买饮料。
text.pinyin: Tā kě le, xiǎng xiān mǎi yǐnliào.
text.english: She has become thirsty and wants to buy a drink first.

LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.exerciseInstruction: Complete each sentence so the new situation is clear.

segments.hint: Put 了 at the end, right after the feeling.

questions.correctFeedback: 餓了 marks the new hungry state.
questions.repairFeedback: Put 了 at the end, right after the feeling.

segments.hint: Put 了 after 來.

questions.correctFeedback: Arrival changes what the group can do now.
questions.repairFeedback: Put 了 after 來.

questions.correctFeedback: The clock has reached ten.

LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_TWO.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_TWO.learnerPromise: Ask how someone travels and answer with transport or walking.
LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_TWO.explanation: Ask with 怎麼. Answer with one travel block before 來 or 去: 坐 + vehicle, 騎腳踏車, or 走路. Add 到 + place for the destination.

teachingGlossary.meaning: do not have; there is not

LESSON_SEVEN_GRAMMAR_TWO.pattern: Person + travel method + 到 + place + 來/去

patternRows.english: I go to school by MRT.
We walk to the post office.
She comes to the hotel by taxi.

items.question: Can you 坐走路 to say you walk somewhere?
items.answer: No. 坐 is only for vehicles: 坐公車, 坐捷運, 坐計程車. Walking is its own travel block — just 走路, no 坐.

items.question: A friend asks 你怎麼去？ Do I answer 我去坐公車 or 我坐公車去?
items.answer: 我坐公車去 — the travel method comes before 去. 我去坐公車 means you are going somewhere to catch the bus.

items.question: How do I ask "How are you going?" — 你為什麼去 or 你怎麼去?
items.answer: 你怎麼去. 怎麼 asks how; 為什麼 asks why, so it fits a reason, not a route.

routeLab.title: Swap the vehicle, keep the route
routeLab.description: Only the How block changes. Destination and direction stay stable.

choices.label: Fast MRT
choices.traditional: 我們坐捷運到飯店去。
choices.simplified: 我们坐捷运到饭店去。
choices.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò jiéyùn dào fàndiàn qù.
choices.english: We take the MRT to the hotel.
choices.note: 坐 introduces public transport and vehicles.

choices.label: Nearby walk
choices.traditional: 我們走路到郵局去。
choices.simplified: 我们走路到邮局去。
choices.pinyin: Wǒmen zǒulù dào yóujú qù.
choices.english: We walk to the post office.
choices.note: 走路 works as a complete travel-method block; do not add 坐.

choices.label: Taxi to airport
choices.traditional: 我們坐計程車到機場去。
choices.simplified: 我们坐计程车到机场去。
choices.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò jìchéngchē dào jīchǎng qù.
choices.english: We take a taxi to the airport.
choices.note: Transport comes before 到 + destination.

routeLab.takeaway: Ask 怎麼去？ Answer with one How block + 到 + destination + 去.

text.traditional: A：你們怎麼去？ B：我們坐公車去。
text.simplified: A：你们怎么去？ B：我们坐公车去。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐmen zěnme qù? B: Wǒmen zuò gōngchē qù.
text.english: A: How are you going? B: By bus.

text.traditional: A：飯店遠不遠？ B：不遠，我們走路去。
text.simplified: A：饭店远不远？ B：不远，我们走路去。

LESSON_SEVEN_PART_ONE.title: Grammar 1–3 · Routes and changing situations

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Draw a Route with 從 and 到
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say where a trip starts, where it ends, and why someone travels.
grammarPages.explanation: 從 is the start pin. 到 is the destination pin. Put each place right after its pin. Finish with 來 or 去. You can add the purpose (the why) at the end.

teachingGlossary.meaning: do not have; there is not

grammarPages.pattern: Person + 從 + start + 到 + destination + 來/去 + purpose

patternRows.english: Go from school to the drink shop to buy something.
Come from the hotel to my home to eat.
Come from Korea to Taiwan to visit a friend.

items.question: I want to say "I go from home to school." Which place comes right after 從?
items.answer: The start — the place you leave. 從 + start, 到 + destination: 我從家到學校去.

right.pinyin: Wǒ cóng jiā dào xuéxiào qù.
right.english: I go from home to school.

items.question: My friend is at the hotel and I am at home. She is coming to my place — 來 or 去?
items.answer: 來. Use 來 when the trip ends where you are; 去 points away from you. Her trip ends at my home, so: 她從飯店到家來.

right.pinyin: Tā cóng fàndiàn dào jiā lái.
right.english: She comes from the hotel to my home.

items.question: English says "go to school." Why is 我去到學校 not right in Chinese?
items.answer: Because 去 already means go, and 到 points at the destination. Chinese puts the place between them: 我到學校去.

routeLab.title: Move the route pins
routeLab.description: Read each trip left to right. Start, destination, direction, then purpose.

choices.label: Go to class
choices.traditional: 我從家到學校去上課。
choices.simplified: 我从家到学校去上课。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ cóng jiā dào xuéxiào qù shàngkè.
choices.english: I go from home to school for class.
choices.note: 從 opens the start. 到 opens the destination. 去 points away from the speaker.

choices.label: Mail a letter
choices.traditional: 我從學校到郵局去寄信。
choices.simplified: 我从学校到邮局去寄信。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ cóng xuéxiào dào yóujú qù jì xìn.
choices.english: I go from school to the post office to mail a letter.
choices.note: The purpose 寄信 comes after the complete route.

choices.label: Visit a friend
choices.traditional: 她從韓國到臺灣來看朋友。
choices.simplified: 她从韩国到台湾来看朋友。
choices.pinyin: Tā cóng Hánguó dào Táiwān lái kàn péngyǒu.
choices.english: She comes from Korea to Taiwan to visit a friend.
choices.note: Use 來 because the trip moves toward the speaker’s viewpoint.

routeLab.takeaway: Pins stay paired: 從 + start, 到 + destination. 來/去 shows which way the trip points, not the vehicle.

text.traditional: A：你從哪裡來？ B：我從飯店來。
text.simplified: A：你从哪里来？ B：我从饭店来。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ cóng nǎlǐ lái? B: Wǒ cóng fàndiàn lái.
text.english: A: Where are you coming from? B: From the hotel.

text.traditional: A：你到哪裡去？ B：我到朋友家去。
text.simplified: A：你到哪里去？ B：我到朋友家去。

text.english: A: Where are you going? B: To my friend’s home.

text.traditional: 我們從學校到超市去買東西。
text.simplified: 我们从学校到超市去买东西。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen cóng xuéxiào dào chāoshì qù mǎi dōngxi.
text.english: We go from school to the supermarket to shop.

examples.teachingNote: Use 來 for motion toward here.

text.simplified: 他明天从饭店到我家来吃饭。
text.pinyin: Tā míngtiān cóng fàndiàn dào wǒ jiā lái chīfàn.
text.english: Tomorrow he will come from the hotel to my home for dinner.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Ask how someone travels and answer with transport or walking.
grammarPages.explanation: Ask with 怎麼. Answer with one travel block before 來 or 去: 坐 + vehicle, 騎腳踏車, or 走路. Add 到 + place for the destination.

teachingGlossary.meaning: do not have; there is not

grammarPages.pattern: Person + travel method + 到 + place + 來/去

patternRows.english: I go to school by MRT.
We walk to the post office.
She comes to the hotel by taxi.

items.question: Can you 坐走路 to say you walk somewhere?
items.answer: No. 坐 is only for vehicles: 坐公車, 坐捷運, 坐計程車. Walking is its own travel block — just 走路, no 坐.

items.question: A friend asks 你怎麼去？ Do I answer 我去坐公車 or 我坐公車去?
items.answer: 我坐公車去 — the travel method comes before 去. 我去坐公車 means you are going somewhere to catch the bus.

items.question: How do I ask "How are you going?" — 你為什麼去 or 你怎麼去?
items.answer: 你怎麼去. 怎麼 asks how; 為什麼 asks why, so it fits a reason, not a route.

routeLab.title: Swap the vehicle, keep the route
routeLab.description: Only the How block changes. Destination and direction stay stable.

choices.label: Fast MRT
choices.traditional: 我們坐捷運到飯店去。
choices.simplified: 我们坐捷运到饭店去。
choices.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò jiéyùn dào fàndiàn qù.
choices.english: We take the MRT to the hotel.
choices.note: 坐 introduces public transport and vehicles.

choices.label: Nearby walk
choices.traditional: 我們走路到郵局去。
choices.simplified: 我们走路到邮局去。
choices.pinyin: Wǒmen zǒulù dào yóujú qù.
choices.english: We walk to the post office.
choices.note: 走路 works as a complete travel-method block; do not add 坐.

choices.label: Taxi to airport
choices.traditional: 我們坐計程車到機場去。
choices.simplified: 我们坐计程车到机场去。
choices.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò jìchéngchē dào jīchǎng qù.
choices.english: We take a taxi to the airport.
choices.note: Transport comes before 到 + destination.

routeLab.takeaway: Ask 怎麼去？ Answer with one How block + 到 + destination + 去.

text.traditional: A：你們怎麼去？ B：我們坐公車去。
text.simplified: A：你们怎么去？ B：我们坐公车去。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐmen zěnme qù? B: Wǒmen zuò gōngchē qù.
text.english: A: How are you going? B: By bus.

text.traditional: A：飯店遠不遠？ B：不遠，我們走路去。
text.simplified: A：饭店远不远？ B：不远，我们走路去。
text.pinyin: A: Fàndiàn yuǎn bù yuǎn? B: Bù yuǎn, wǒmen zǒulù qù.
text.english: A: Is the hotel far? B: No, let’s walk.

text.traditional: 她坐計程車到機場去。
text.simplified: 她坐计程车到机场去。
text.pinyin: Tā zuò jìchéngchē dào jīchǎng qù.
text.english: She takes a taxi to the airport.

text.traditional: A：友美怎麼來？ B：她騎腳踏車來。
text.simplified: A：友美怎么来？ B：她骑脚踏车来。
text.pinyin: A: Yǒuměi zěnme lái? B: Tā qí jiǎotàchē lái.
text.english: A: How is Youmei coming? B: By bicycle.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Put 了 at the end when a new situation becomes true.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 了 at the end of the sentence when something new happens. Before, it was not true; now it is. 了 can come after a feeling, a time, an arrival, or a new chance to act. 了 does not mean "past time".

teachingGlossary.meaning: do not have; there is not

patternRows.english: I have become tired.
It is ten o’clock now.
The bus is here; we can board now.

items.question: Your stomach just started growling. Which tells people "I have become hungry"?
items.answer: 我餓了. 了 says the hungry state is new; 我很餓 only describes how hungry you are.

items.question: The bus is here and we can board. Where does 了 go in 我們可以上車?
items.answer: At the very end: 我們可以上車了. 了 closes the whole new situation — not between 可以 and 上車.

right.english: We can board the bus now.

items.question: Someone asks if you are tired now, after the long walk. Do you answer 我昨天累了?
items.answer: No — that says you were tired yesterday. Say 我現在累了: 了 marks the change, and the time word tells when.

discoveryLab.title: Ring the change bell
discoveryLab.description: See the moment when a state becomes true for the first time.

choices.label: Hungry now
choices.traditional: 我餓了。
choices.simplified: 我饿了。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ è le.
choices.english: I’m hungry now.
choices.note: The speaker was not hungry before; that state has changed.

choices.label: Bus arrived
choices.traditional: 公車來了。
choices.simplified: 公车来了。
choices.pinyin: Gōngchē lái le.
choices.english: The bus is here now.
choices.note: The arrival creates a new situation.

choices.label: Time changed
choices.traditional: 現在十點了。
choices.simplified: 现在十点了。
choices.pinyin: Xiànzài shí diǎn le.
choices.english: It’s ten now.
choices.note: The clock has reached a new reference point.

choices.label: Repair meaning
choices.traditional: 昨天我累了 → 我現在累了
choices.simplified: 昨天我累了 → 我现在累了
choices.pinyin: Zuótiān wǒ lèi le → Wǒ xiànzài lèi le
choices.english: I am tired now.
choices.note: For this target meaning, make the changed situation current and clear.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Use 了 when "now it is different" matters.

text.traditional: 我累了，不想走了。
text.simplified: 我累了，不想走了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ lèi le, bù xiǎng zǒu le.
text.english: I’m tired now and no longer want to walk.

text.traditional: 公車來了，我們可以上車了。
text.simplified: 公车来了，我们可以上车了。
text.pinyin: Gōngchē lái le, wǒmen kěyǐ shàngchē le.
text.english: The bus is here; now we can board.

text.traditional: 現在十點了，我們先回家吧。
text.simplified: 现在十点了，我们先回家吧。
text.pinyin: Xiànzài shí diǎn le, wǒmen xiān huí jiā ba.
text.english: It’s ten now; let’s go home first.

text.traditional: 她渴了，想先買飲料。
text.simplified: 她渴了，想先买饮料。
text.pinyin: Tā kě le, xiǎng xiān mǎi yǐnliào.
text.english: She has become thirsty and wants to buy a drink first.

dialogue.title: 對話一 · Dialogue 1
dialogue.setting: 上課前商量明天去天美飯店 · Planning tomorrow’s trip to Tianmei Hotel before class

text.traditional: 元真，我們明天幾點去找妳的韓國朋友？
text.simplified: 元真，我们明天几点去找妳的韩国朋友？
text.pinyin: Yuánzhēn, wǒmen míngtiān jǐ diǎn qù zhǎo nǐ de Hánguó péngyǒu?
text.english: Yuanzhen, what time are we going to meet up with your Korean friends tomorrow?

text.traditional: 我們下午四點要到天美飯店，她在那裡等我們。
text.simplified: 我们下午四点要到天美饭店，她在那里等我们。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen xiàwǔ sì diǎn yào dào Tiānměi Fàndiàn, tā zài nàli děng wǒmen.
text.english: We have to arrive at Tianmei Hotel at 4 in the afternoon. She will wait for us there.

text.traditional: 我們要怎麼去？坐捷運還是坐公車？
text.simplified: 我们要怎么去？坐捷运还是坐公车？
text.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zěnme qù? Zuò jiéyùn háishì zuò gōngchē?
text.english: How do we get there? By MRT or bus?

text.traditional: 聽說那家飯店不遠，我想我們可以從學校走路去。
text.simplified: 听说那家饭店不远，我想我们可以从学校走路去。
text.pinyin: Tīngshuō nà jiā fàndiàn bù yuǎn, wǒ xiǎng wǒmen kěyǐ cóng xuéxiào zǒulù qù.
text.english: I heard that the hotel is not far; I think we can go there from the school on foot.

text.traditional: 可是我不知道怎麼走，妳知道嗎？
text.simplified: 可是我不知道怎么走，妳知道吗？
text.pinyin: Kěshì wǒ bù zhīdào zěnme zǒu, nǐ zhīdào ma?

text.traditional: 我也不知道。我們可以先上網看地圖。
text.simplified: 我也不知道。我们可以先上网看地图。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yě bù zhīdào. Wǒmen kěyǐ xiān shàngwǎng kàn dìtú.
text.english: I don’t know either. We can check the map online first.

text.traditional: 啊！上課了！我們先上課吧。
text.simplified: 啊！上课了！我们先上课吧。
text.pinyin: A! Shàngkè le! Wǒmen xiān shàngkè ba.
text.english: Ah! The class has started! Let’s go to class now.

text.traditional: 好。
text.simplified: 好。
text.pinyin: Hǎo.
text.english: Okay.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Name an activity first, then comment on it.
grammarPages.explanation: In Chinese, you can say the activity first, then say what you think about it. Think: activity → your comment.

teachingGlossary.meaning: do not have; there is not

patternRows.english: Taking the MRT is convenient.
Walking there is too slow.
I like both running and swimming.

items.question: In English I say "It’s convenient to take the MRT." Does Chinese copy that order?
items.answer: No. Say the activity first, then the comment: 坐捷運很方便. The activity is what you are talking about; the comment follows.

items.question: Do I need 是 between the activity and the comment — 走路去是太慢了?
items.answer: No. Put the activity first and the describing word right after it: 走路去太慢了. 是 is not needed here.

items.question: I like running, swimming, and tennis. Where does 都 go?
items.answer: Right after the person, before the action: 我都喜歡. Never after the verb: 我喜歡都跑步 is wrong.

right.traditional: 跑步、游泳、打網球，我都喜歡。
right.simplified: 跑步、游泳、打网球，我都喜欢。
right.pinyin: Pǎobù, yóuyǒng, dǎ wǎngqiú, wǒ dōu xǐhuān.
right.english: Running, swimming, and tennis — I like them all.

discoveryLab.title: Put the activity on stage
discoveryLab.description: The first chunk is what we are talking about; the rest is the comment.

choices.label: MRT
choices.traditional: 坐捷運很方便。
choices.simplified: 坐捷运很方便。
choices.pinyin: Zuò jiéyùn hěn fāngbiàn.
choices.english: Taking the MRT is convenient.
choices.note: 坐捷運 is the activity topic; 很方便 is the comment.

choices.label: Walking
choices.traditional: 走路去太慢了。
choices.simplified: 走路去太慢了。
choices.pinyin: Zǒulù qù tài màn le.
choices.english: Walking there is too slow.
choices.note: 走路去 is evaluated as one complete activity.

choices.label: Three sports
choices.traditional: 跑步、游泳、打網球，我都喜歡。
choices.simplified: 跑步、游泳、打网球，我都喜欢。
choices.pinyin: Pǎobù, yóuyǒng, dǎ wǎngqiú, wǒ dōu xǐhuān.
choices.english: Running, swimming, and tennis—I like them all.
choices.note: Several activities can share one comment.

choices.label: Repair focus
choices.traditional: 很方便坐捷運 → 坐捷運很方便
choices.simplified: 很方便坐捷运 → 坐捷运很方便
choices.pinyin: Hěn fāngbiàn zuò jiéyùn → Zuò jiéyùn hěn fāngbiàn
choices.english: Taking the MRT is convenient.
choices.note: Put the activity before the comment.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Activity first, comment second. You do not need 是 between them.

text.traditional: 坐公車很便宜，可是有一點慢。
text.simplified: 坐公车很便宜，可是有一点慢。
text.pinyin: Zuò gōngchē hěn piányi, kěshì yǒu yìdiǎn màn.
text.english: Taking the bus is inexpensive, but a little slow.

text.traditional: 走路去太慢了，我們坐捷運吧。
text.simplified: 走路去太慢了，我们坐捷运吧。
text.pinyin: Zǒulù qù tài màn le, wǒmen zuò jiéyùn ba.
text.english: Walking is too slow; let’s take the MRT.

text.traditional: 唱歌、跳舞，她都喜歡。
text.simplified: 唱歌、跳舞，她都喜欢。
text.pinyin: Chànggē, tiàowǔ, tā dōu xǐhuān.
text.english: Singing and dancing—she likes both.

text.traditional: 住在學校附近很方便。
text.simplified: 住在学校附近很方便。
text.pinyin: Zhù zài xuéxiào fùjìn hěn fāngbiàn.
text.english: Living near school is convenient.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe two qualities or abilities that are true at the same time.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 又 before each quality: 又快又方便. Both sides describe the same person or thing, and they match in shape. Use 又…又… for two qualities that are true at the same time — not for two things.

teachingGlossary.meaning: do not have; there is not

grammarPages.pattern: Person or thing + 又 + quality 1 + 又 + quality 2

patternRows.english: The MRT is both fast and convenient.
A taxi is both fast and comfortable.
She is both cute and pretty.

items.question: Do I need 又 twice for "fast and convenient"?
items.answer: Yes — one 又 for each quality: 又快又方便. Each quality gets its own 又.

right.english: The MRT is fast and convenient.

items.question: Can I say 附近又學校又店 for "there is a school and a shop nearby"?
items.answer: No. 又…又… pairs qualities, not places or things. For two places, use 有…也有…: 附近有學校，也有店.

right.pinyin: Fùjìn yǒu xuéxiào, yě yǒu diàn.
right.english: There is a school and a shop nearby.

items.question: Can I mix 又 and 也 — 公車又快也便宜?
items.answer: No. Pair both qualities with 又: 又快又便宜. 也 adds a separate point; it does not build the pair.

right.english: The bus is fast and cheap.

discoveryLab.title: Balance the two sides
discoveryLab.description: Each 又 opens one matching description. Both sides describe the same person or thing.

choices.label: Transit
choices.traditional: 臺北的捷運又快又方便。
choices.simplified: 台北的捷运又快又方便。
choices.pinyin: Táiběi de jiéyùn yòu kuài yòu fāngbiàn.
choices.english: Taipei’s MRT is fast and convenient.
choices.note: 快 and 方便 are two matching qualities.

choices.label: Person
choices.traditional: 我同學的妹妹又可愛又漂亮。
choices.simplified: 我同学的妹妹又可爱又漂亮。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ tóngxué de mèimei yòu kě’ài yòu piàoliang.
choices.english: My classmate’s younger sister is cute and pretty.
choices.note: One person has both qualities.

choices.label: Two states
choices.traditional: 我現在又餓又渴。
choices.simplified: 我现在又饿又渴。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài yòu è yòu kě.
choices.english: I am both hungry and thirsty now.
choices.note: Both body states are true together.

choices.label: Repair balance
choices.traditional: 捷運又快方便 → 捷運又快又方便
choices.simplified: 捷运又快方便 → 捷运又快又方便
choices.pinyin: Jiéyùn yòu kuài fāngbiàn → Jiéyùn yòu kuài yòu fāngbiàn
choices.english: The MRT is both fast and convenient.
choices.note: Give each quality its own 又.

discoveryLab.takeaway: One person or thing, two matching 又 blocks.

text.traditional: 這家飯店又便宜又舒服。
text.simplified: 这家饭店又便宜又舒服。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiā fàndiàn yòu piányi yòu shūfu.
text.english: This hotel is inexpensive and comfortable.

text.traditional: 坐計程車又快又方便，可是比較貴。
text.simplified: 坐计程车又快又方便，可是比较贵。
text.pinyin: Zuò jìchéngchē yòu kuài yòu fāngbiàn, kěshì bǐjiào guì.
text.english: Taking a taxi is fast and convenient, but more expensive.

text.traditional: 元真又會唱歌又會跳舞。
text.simplified: 元真又会唱歌又会跳舞。
text.pinyin: Yuánzhēn yòu huì chànggē yòu huì tiàowǔ.
text.english: Yuanzhen can both sing and dance.

text.traditional: 我現在又累又渴，想先休息。
text.simplified: 我现在又累又渴，想先休息。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài yòu lèi yòu kě, xiǎng xiān xiūxí.
text.english: I am tired and thirsty now and want to rest first.

grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Choose a complete 又…又… pair for each scene.

segments.hint: Build 又 + 快 + 又 + 方便.

questions.correctFeedback: Both qualities get their own 又.
questions.repairFeedback: Build 又 + 快 + 又 + 方便.

segments.hint: Put 又 immediately before each quality.

questions.correctFeedback: The hotel has both qualities.
questions.repairFeedback: Put 又 immediately before each quality.

segments.hint: Use one 又 before 餓 and one before 渴.

questions.correctFeedback: Both new body states are true together.
questions.repairFeedback: Use one 又 before 餓 and one before 渴.

dialogue.title: 對話二 · Dialogue 2
dialogue.setting: 看地圖決定怎麼去飯店 · Reading the map to decide how to get to the hotel

text.traditional: 友美，妳看，天美飯店在大學路。我現在知道怎麼走了。
text.simplified: 友美，妳看，天美饭店在大学路。我现在知道怎么走了。
text.pinyin: Yǒuměi, nǐ kàn, Tiānměi Fàndiàn zài Dàxué Lù. Wǒ xiànzài zhīdào zěnme zǒu le.
text.english: Look, Youmei. Tianmei Hotel is on Daxue Road. Now I know how to get there.

text.traditional: （看地圖）啊！天美飯店在這裡！我知道這個地方，附近有郵局跟超級市場。
text.simplified: （看地图）啊！天美饭店在这里！我知道这个地方，附近有邮局跟超级市场。
text.pinyin: (Kàn dìtú) A! Tiānměi Fàndiàn zài zhèlǐ! Wǒ zhīdào zhè ge dìfang, fùjìn yǒu yóujú gēn chāojíshìchǎng.
text.english: (Looking at the map) Ah! So here is Tianmei Hotel! I know this place. There is a post office and a supermarket nearby.

text.traditional: 我想走路去一定沒問題。
text.simplified: 我想走路去一定没问题。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zǒulù qù yídìng méi wèntí.
text.english: I think it will certainly be okay going there on foot.

text.traditional: 可是我覺得那裡有點兒遠，走路去太累了。
text.simplified: 可是我觉得那里有点儿远，走路去太累了。
text.pinyin: Kěshì wǒ juéde nàlǐ yǒudiǎnr yuǎn, zǒulù qù tài lèi le.
text.english: But I think it’s a bit far. It’s too tiring to get there on foot.

text.traditional: 妳想怎麼去？
text.simplified: 妳想怎么去？
text.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng zěnme qù?
text.english: How do you want to get there?

text.traditional: 坐捷運又方便又舒服，我們可以坐捷運。
text.simplified: 坐捷运又方便又舒服，我们可以坐捷运。
text.pinyin: Zuò jiéyùn yòu fāngbiàn yòu shūfu, wǒmen kěyǐ zuò jiéyùn.
text.english: Taking the MRT is convenient and comfortable. We can take the MRT.

text.traditional: 好，我們明天坐捷運去吧。
text.simplified: 好，我们明天坐捷运去吧。
text.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒmen míngtiān zuò jiéyùn qù ba.
text.english: Ok, let’s take the MRT to get there tomorrow.

comprehension.hint: Find the paired qualities in Youmei’s answer.
